text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's Justice, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs minister Emmerson Mnangagwa, whose government is facing international pressure to abolish the death penalty, said on Wednesday he was personally opposed to capital punishment.

- Two local businesses have submitted applications to Zimbabwe's finance ministry for permission to establish commercial banks. If approved, this will bring to seven the number of such institutions in the southern African country.
- The government says it will press ahead with plans to acquire over Z$2 billion worth of land for resettlement regardless of worth. Britain and other donors have agreed to fund the programme.
- The Zimbabwe Mining Development Corporation (ZMDC) is closing its loss-making Lomagundi smelting and mining company near the northern town of Chinhoyi, a move which will cost 750 people their jobs.

- Minority shareholders in the state-owned Zimbabwe iron and steel company, Zisco, have been given an option to either sell their stakes or express an intent to increase their shareholding as the government steps up its plans to divest from the steelworks.

- Zimbabwe's state-owned Grain Marketing Board (GMB), which has been battling to pay farmers for maize delivered to it, now has the capacity to do so and farmers should expect their money just in time for the new planting season.

- There were no significant changes in the situation at Harare's two main referral hospitals on Wednesday where several wards remained closed as the month-old strike by junior doctors and nurses demanding salary rises and improved working conditions continued.
- State-owned Air Zimbabwe has spend about Z$3 million on spare parts for aircrafts this year and the airline believes a waiver of customs duty by the government would cut its costs considerably.
